name: Ötzi Dorf
kurzbeschreibung: Archaeological open-air park in Umhausen in the Ötztal valley, vividly reconstructing Neolithic life and culture during Ötzi the Iceman's era.
preis: Erwachsene ca. 12,00 €, Kinder ca. 6,50 €, Kombiticket mit Greifvogelpark möglich
beschreibung:
Überblick

The Ötzi-Dorf in Umhausen in Tyrol's Ötztal valley is a fascinating archaeological open-air park that vividly introduces visitors to the daily life, housing, and subsistence of Neolithic communities. Around 4,000 BC, the world-famous Iceman lived here before his mummified body was discovered at Tisenjoch in 1991. Covering an area of roughly 9,000 square metres, prehistoric huts, storage facilities, workshops, and ritual grounds have been reconstructed in close cooperation with the University of Innsbruck. Situated right at the foot of the roaring Stuibenfall waterfall, Ötzi-Dorf combines scientific authenticity with an engaging outdoor experience for families.

Route & Anforderungen

The extensive circular trail through the open-air grounds leads past reconstructed dwellings, toolmaking workshops, baking ovens, and enclosures featuring ancient domestic animal breeds dating back to prehistoric times, such as Przewalski horses, Soay sheep, and Mangalica pigs. The path is completely level with well-maintained gravel trails, making it fully barrier-free and accessible for strollers and wheelchairs. Exploring the park and its interactive demonstration stations takes around two to three hours. Dogs are welcome on the grounds when kept on a short leash.

Besuch & Anreise

The open-air museum is open annually from early May until late October, daily from 09:30 to 17:30 (with extended summer hours until 18:30). Standard admission is around 12.00 Euro for adults and 6.50 Euro for children; a combined ticket with the adjacent Umhausen Birds of Prey Park is available. By car, take the Inntal motorway A12 to the Ötztal exit, then continue along the B186 federal road to Umhausen. Ample parking is available at the Bischoffsplatz car park. By public transport, take the train to Ötztal railway station and connect to bus route 4194 to Umhausen Feuerwehr, followed by an easy ten-minute stroll.

Tipps

Visiting during special demonstration days is highly recommended, when skilled craftsmen show historic techniques such as flintknapping, traditional fire-making, archery, and prehistoric pottery. You can round off your day trip by continuing onto the hiking trail to Stuibenfall, Tyrol's highest waterfall, or watching the falconry flight shows next door.
